name: JFrog Ltd.

profile.description: JFrog Ltd., founded in 2008 and headquartered in Sunnyvale, California (with major R&D in Israel), provides a software supply chain platform built around JFrog Artifactory, the universal binary repository, plus Xray and Advanced Security scanning, Distribution, Pipelines and an ML model registry gained through the 2025 Qwak acquisition [4][3]. Q2 2026 revenue rose 28.7% YoY to $163.8M, with cloud revenue up 53% to $87.5M; FY2026 revenue guidance was raised to $648-652M (~22% growth) and Q3 guidance is $164-166M [1]. The stock trades at $94.39 (52-week range $34.05-$105.76) for an ~$11.4B market cap [4].

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): JFrog has extended Artifactory into a broader DevSecOps platform (Xray, Advanced Security, Distribution) and shifted toward cloud, with cloud revenue of $87.5M now over half of Q2 2026 revenue and growing 53% YoY [1]. Revenue grew from $150.8M in 2020 to $531.8M in 2025 [4]. AI Deployment (1/2): JFrog acquired Qwak for ~$230M in 2025 to add MLOps and positions itself as 'the model registry for the AI-driven world', but has not quantified AI revenue or savings [3]. Market Share (2/2): Artifactory is the de facto universal artifact repository standard, and net dollar retention is guided at a 120% floor for 2026 [1]. Product Pipeline (1/2): Cloud growth guidance was raised to 41-43% (from 30-32%) and security/AI governance are expanding, but no dated next-generation launches with revenue visibility were disclosed [1]. R&D Intensity (1/1): TTM R&D is 35% of revenue ($195.1M in FY2025), top quartile for software [4].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): The 'Liquid Software' vision of software flowing continuously and securely from developer to device is clear and distinctive in DevOps but describes a technical outcome rather than a deeper purpose [3]. Community Impact (1/2): JFrog offers free Artifactory for open-source projects, runs the swampUP developer conference, has published ESG reports since 2023 and created a chief sustainability officer function, but no distinctive dollar-quantified giving program was found [5]. Employee Retention (0/2): No tenure or voluntary turnover data was found; headcount is ~1,800 [4]. Insider Buying (0/2): FMP insider statistics show zero open-market purchases against more than 200 insider sales from Q4 2025 through Q4 2026 to date [4]; stock-based compensation runs at 27% of revenue, a dilution signal rather than insider conviction [4].

infrastructure.label: DEVELOPING
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored as a Growth stock (10 weight units). The balance sheet is pristine (D/E 1.5%, cash ~$6.77/share) and scores 1.0, and both Q2 2026 revenue growth of 28.7% and the 2020-2025 revenue CAGR of 28.7% score 1.0 (the CAGR at 2x weight) [4]. However, JFrog remains GAAP unprofitable: TTM ROE of -4.9% scores 0 at 2x weight and TTM net margin of -7.3% scores 0 [4]. Forward P/E of 82.4 (price $94.39 / FY2027 consensus non-GAAP EPS $1.15) exceeds the 60x floor and scores 0, and FMP's forward PEG of -10.7 (negative on GAAP earnings) scores 0 at 2x weight [4]. Weighted 4.0/10 = 4. Liquidity is ample at ~1.9M shares/day (~$178M daily).

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (7/9): PROTECTED. Investors increasingly distinguish JFrog's software-infrastructure role from conventional SaaS exposed to AI disruption, and CEO Shlomi Ben Haim argues AI agents amplify developer output and therefore raise demand for artifact management and security scanning [3]. The 53% cloud growth and 120% NDR floor support that view, though platform players (GitHub, GitLab, cloud hyperscalers) could bundle competing registries [1]. AI Opportunity (0/1): JFrog sells ML model management (via Qwak) and AI governance features, but has not disclosed specific AI revenue, so the tiebreaker is withheld [3].

infinite_game.summary: JFrog has held one consistent idea, 'Liquid Software', since 2008 and has kept investing (35% of revenue in R&D) through persistent GAAP losses to build a cloud and security platform [3][4]. Through Sinek's lens, though, that idea is a product vision rather than a Just Cause people sacrifice for, the cloud shift has been incremental evolution, and there is no clear evidence of high-trust culture or an improve-not-win stance toward rivals.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): 'Liquid Software' has been the company's north star since founding and differentiates it from generic DevOps vendors [3]. But it describes what the product does rather than a better future state for others, so Sinek would classify it as a mission statement.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Leadership has funded R&D at $195.1M (37% of FY2025 revenue) while running GAAP net losses of $69M-$90M per year since 2022, paid ~$230M for Qwak to build AI capability, and deliberately pruned lower-value customers to focus on large enterprises [4][3]. These are long-term bets, but they rest on a large SBC budget rather than visible personal sacrifice.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Co-founder Shlomi Ben Haim has led JFrog since 2008, providing continuity, and the company has grown to ~1,800 employees without major layoff headlines [4][3]. No tenure or turnover data was found to evidence an exceptional Circle of Safety.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): JFrog has moved from a self-hosted binary repository toward a cloud-first DevSecOps and MLOps platform, with cloud now over 50% of revenue [1]. This is meaningful evolution, but the Artifactory core remains the center of the business rather than having been abandoned for a new model.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): Ben Haim frames JFrog's AI strategy as 'judge us by the friends we keep' (partnerships with GitHub, NVIDIA and hyperscalers), but no management commentary was found crediting rivals' strengths as a driver of self-improvement [3].

investment_thesis: JFrog is accelerating: Q2 2026 revenue grew 28.7% to $163.8M, cloud revenue grew 53% to $87.5M, FY2026 guidance was raised to $648-652M and cloud growth guidance to 41-43%, with gross margin guided at 82-83% and NDR at a 120% floor [1]. The balance sheet carries almost no debt (D/E 1.5%) and TTM free cash flow is ~$1.39/share, while consensus expects non-GAAP EPS to rise from $0.98 in 2026 to $1.15 in 2027 [4]. AI-driven code generation increases the volume of artifacts and models that need versioning and security scanning, which is why investors treat JFrog as AI-resilient infrastructure rather than disruptable SaaS [3]. Its Inspire score of 43 (ALIGNED) carries no negative attributions.
thesis_continued: The bear case is valuation and earnings quality. At $94.39 the stock trades at ~19x TTM sales and ~82x FY2027 non-GAAP EPS, and GAAP results remain negative (TTM net margin -7.3%, ROE -4.9%) because stock-based compensation consumes ~27% of revenue [4]. The stock has nearly tripled from its $34.05 52-week low, so any slowdown from the ~29% growth rate could compress the multiple sharply. GitHub, GitLab and the hyperscalers can bundle package registries and security scanning, and a 2025 OpenAI-related vulnerability episode shows the security exposure that comes with being a supply-chain chokepoint [3].
key_catalysts: Q3 2026 results (early November) against guidance of $164-166M revenue and $0.22-0.24 non-GAAP EPS, with cloud growth tracking the raised 41-43% full-year outlook [1]
AI-generated code and model proliferation driving consumption of Artifactory, Xray and the Qwak-derived ML model registry, supporting the 120% NDR floor [1][3]
Mix shift to cloud and rising scale moving GAAP results toward breakeven: Q2 2026 GAAP net loss narrowed to $4.2M from $21.7M a year earlier [4]
key_risks: Valuation: ~19x TTM sales and ~82x FY2027 consensus EPS leaves no margin of safety if cloud growth decelerates from 53% [4]
Persistent GAAP losses and heavy dilution: stock-based compensation is ~27% of revenue and FY2025 GAAP net loss was $71.8M despite strong non-GAAP margins [4]
Platform bundling by GitHub, GitLab, AWS, Azure and Google Cloud, plus software supply chain security incidents, could erode Artifactory's position as the neutral system of record [3]
